title: Circuit Breakers (Resilience4j)
summary: Stop sending ordinary traffic to an unhealthy dependency, probe recovery deliberately, and protect the rest of the agent workflow from repeated failure.
overview: A circuit breaker observes dependency outcomes and temporarily rejects calls when configured failure or slow-call conditions indicate poor health. Closed permits calls, open rejects them, and half-open allows a limited recovery sample. It is distinct from a timeout, retry policy, rate limiter, or concurrency bulkhead; those controls address different failure dimensions.

Resilience4j provides configurable count-based or time-based sliding windows, minimum call counts, failure and slow-call thresholds, and half-open behavior. Choose failure classification carefully. A user's invalid request should not normally declare the entire dependency unhealthy, and a breaker does not cancel calls already in flight.

production.poc: A prototype can simulate dependency errors and observe state transitions. Avoid selecting production thresholds from a handful of successful demo calls.
production.production: Production tunes windows and minimum samples to actual traffic, scopes breakers by dependency or meaningful failure domain, and defines a useful open-state response.
production.scale: At scale, too many fine-grained breakers create state and metric cardinality, while one global breaker can spread a localized outage. Test recovery under load and ensure probes do not all arrive simultaneously across instances.

components.name: Outcome classifier
components.role: Distinguishes dependency failures and slow calls from expected business rejections.

components.name: Sliding-window recorder
components.role: Tracks the sample used to evaluate configured failure and latency conditions.

components.name: Breaker state
components.role: Controls closed, open, and limited half-open admission.

components.name: Fallback handler
components.role: Returns cached, partial, queued, or unavailable results according to business policy.

components.name: State telemetry
components.role: Exposes transitions, rejected calls, sample counts, and recovery behavior.

flow.title: Classify call
flow.description: Select the breaker for the dependency and operation's actual failure domain.

flow.title: Check admission
flow.description: Permit normal traffic when closed, reject when open, or allocate a half-open probe.

flow.title: Execute bounded request
flow.description: Apply a separate timeout and concurrency control to the admitted call.

flow.title: Record outcome
flow.description: Count configured failures and slow calls while excluding expected business responses.

flow.title: Transition state
flow.description: Open only after the required sample and thresholds are met, then wait according to recovery policy.

flow.title: Probe and restore
flow.description: Admit limited tests, close after acceptable results, or reopen when the dependency remains unhealthy.

diagrams.title: Circuit breaker recovery states
diagrams.code:
stateDiagram-v2
 [*] --> Closed
 Closed --> Open: Minimum sample and failure threshold met
 Open --> HalfOpen: Recovery wait completed
 HalfOpen --> Closed: Probe outcomes acceptable
 HalfOpen --> Open: Probe outcomes unhealthy
 Closed --> Closed: Record admitted call outcomes
 Open --> Open: Reject ordinary calls
diagrams.caption: A separate timeout bounds each admitted call; the breaker controls whether new calls are attempted.

useCase.title: Protecting an itinerary assistant from a failing inventory API
useCase.situation: A travel platform's assistant checks hotel inventory while assembling business-trip options.
useCase.problem: A slow supplier endpoint causes repeated waits and consumes worker capacity across unrelated itinerary requests.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must stop overloading the supplier and continue with clearly identified available evidence.
useCase.architecture: A supplier-scoped breaker records relevant errors and slow calls, while timeouts and bulkheads protect individual requests and worker capacity.
runtime: When the configured health conditions are met, the breaker opens and the assistant excludes unverified supplier inventory.
After the recovery interval, limited probes test the supplier before normal traffic resumes.
useCase.failure: If probes fail, the breaker reopens and the itinerary remains explicit about missing inventory rather than showing stale availability as current.
useCase.impact: Track state duration, rejected calls, probe outcomes, and unaffected supplier latency. A breaker improves containment, not the failed dependency itself.

tradeoffs.benefit: Workers avoid repeatedly waiting on a known unhealthy service.
tradeoffs.cost: Some calls that might have succeeded are rejected.

tradeoffs.benefit: Local failures have a smaller blast radius.
Degradation can be detected before complete failure.
tradeoffs.cost: Poor tuning can open the breaker during legitimate long operations.

failures.scenario: Low traffic produces misleading failure percentages
failures.detection: Minimum sample requirements are not met or samples are unrepresentative.
failures.recovery: Tune windows and minimum calls to observed demand.

failures.scenario: Business validation errors open the breaker
failures.detection: Outcome classification counts caller mistakes as dependency failures.
failures.recovery: Exclude expected rejections and retain separate business metrics.

mistakes.mistake: Using a breaker as a concurrency limit
mistakes.fix: Add a bulkhead or semaphore for in-flight capacity.

mistakes.mistake: Retrying immediately when the breaker is open
mistakes.fix: Respect the open-state policy and avoid retry amplification.

mistakes.mistake: Sharing one breaker across unrelated suppliers
mistakes.fix: Scope health to the actual dependency boundary.

whenToUse: A remote dependency can fail repeatedly or become slow.
Fast rejection enables a meaningful degraded response.
Sufficient traffic exists to estimate health sensibly.
whenNotToUse: Failures are independent caller validation errors.
Every rejected call would trigger more uncontrolled retries.
No operational owner can tune and observe recovery.
checklist: Set minimum sample and window type.
Pair with timeouts and concurrency limits.
Test fallback and recovery under load.
